clips.title: AWS re:Invent 2022 - Minimizing the production impact of ML model updates w/shadow testing (AIM343)
clips.why: Shadow testing is the general name for our observe mode: the new thing runs on real traffic next to the old one, and only the old one's answer is used.
look: The new version gets a copy of real requests, but its answers are not served to users.
The point is to compare the two side by side before you switch.
Switching is a decision made from the comparison, not from the calendar.
clips.after: In fcp the sniff is the shadow and the full review is the one we serve. Every push gives us one side-by-side pair.

clips.title: Understanding Confidence Intervals: Statistics Help
clips.why: A calm, clear explanation of what a confidence interval says, and why it gets narrower as the sample grows.
look: A confidence interval is a range for the true value, not a promise about one number.
What makes the interval wide or narrow.
Sample size: more examples, a narrower interval. That is our 'wait another week'.
clips.after: Our bar uses the top of that range, so a sniff with few examples cannot pass by luck.

clips.title: Wilson Score Interval — Confidence Intervals Explained in 2 Minutes
clips.why: The specific interval our go-live check uses, and why it works for small samples and rates close to zero.
look: Why the simple interval breaks for small samples and rates near 0% or 100%.
How Wilson moves the centre and keeps the range sensible.
Rates near zero are exactly our case: we hope the sniff is almost never wrong.
clips.after: wilsonUpper in the lab is this formula; we only use its upper end and compare it with 2%.

practice.q: Complete the one-line policy change that takes fcp's sniff live.
practice.why: With observe false, a push whose open findings are all fulfilled and sure gets the short sniff line instead of a full review.

practice.q: A sniff answer says fulfilled with confidence 0.80. fcp's fulfilConfidence is 0.85. What does live mode do with this push?

options.text: Skips the full review, because the answer is fulfilled
options.why: Fulfilled is not enough. The answer must also be sure, which means at least 0.85.

options.text: Runs the full review, because the answer is not sure
options.why: Below 0.85 the sniff is not trusted, so the full review runs as today.

options.text: Asks the sniff again with a bigger model
options.why: There is no second sniff. Not sure simply means a full review.

practice.q: Which result lets the sniff go live?

options.text: 0 wrong of 60 sure answers, skip rate 60%
options.why: The upper bound is about 6%, above the 2% bar.

options.text: 1 wrong of 300 sure answers, skip rate 67%
options.why: The upper bound is about 1.9% and the skip rate is above 40%: both bars hold.

options.text: 0 wrong of 300 sure answers, skip rate 30%
options.why: Safe, but it would skip too few reviews to be worth the switch.

practice.q: Put the road from observe mode to live in order.
items: The sniff runs in observe mode and every answer is paired with a full review
Count false fulfilled answers and the skip rate from the pairs
Compare the Wilson upper bound with 2% and the skip rate with 40%
If both hold, open the one-line PR that sets observe to false
Watch the re-flag rate for two weeks and switch back above 2%
practice.why: The data comes first, the decision follows the bars, and the switch is watched afterwards, because live data can differ from the past.

practice.q: A reviewer asks Byte to fix two findings with @byte-fix, the author merges the fix, and the same reviewer approves the PR to main. With the Requested-by trailer in place, what does the check on main do?

options.text: Passes: the reviewer is not the PR author
options.why: The reviewer asked for code in this PR, so they joined the requester set through the trailer.

options.text: Fails until someone outside the requester set approves after the last fix commit
options.why: The check reads Requested-by from Byte's fix commits and accepts only a newer approval from someone who asked for none of the code.

options.text: Fails forever, because Byte's code can never reach main
options.why: Fix PRs reach main all the time. They need the right approval, not a ban.
